questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink fast, alcohol builds up in your body quickly. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your system after that hour.

questions.question: If you pass parked vehicles on your right with no oncoming traffic, ride:

options.text: On the left side of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked vehicles on your right with no oncoming traffic. This helps you avoid dangers like opening car doors and people stepping out between vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane for more space around you.

questions.question: While riding, your normal scanning should include:

options.text: Looking in the rearview mirror constantly.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of normal scanning. Also check your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: For group riding, the best formation for keeping riders together with safe space is:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps riders close together while giving each rider enough space cushion around them.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should include everything except:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands. Paint inspection is not needed.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and stay off the brakes.
Shift weight to the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel and immediately leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and keep a straight course if a tire goes flat. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Slow down before leaving the road.

questions.question: Wearing what gives you the best chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best defense against injury. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face from injury in a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, you will:
questions.explanation: You must shift into higher gears as your motorcycle's speed increases.

questions.question: Which one does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC is determined by body weight, how much alcohol is consumed, and how fast it is consumed. How often someone drinks does not affect BAC. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Before riding, check your motorcycle's clutch. A clutch that works properly should feel:
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when you release it. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle rider has an advantage because:

options.text: The motorcycle can speed up faster than a car.
The rider can move to the left side of the lane to avoid opening doors and people stepping out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider can move to the left side of the lane to avoid opening doors and people stepping out.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, ride in the left part of your lane. This helps you avoid car doors opening, people getting out, or people stepping between vehicles. Only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light will change to red soon.
The traffic light will change to green soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light will change to red soon.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal is about to turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: When it starts raining, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is usually best, but this depends on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: Service signs are:
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous because:

options.text: The vehicle could block your way to escape.
Other drivers can easily see the motorcycle.
You may not see road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle could block your way to escape.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is risky. The other vehicle could swerve into your lane and hit you. It could also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection:

options.text: Should only be done by a mechanic.

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. A pre-ride inspection takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When riding at night, keep a minimum following distance of:
questions.explanation: In the dark, it is hard to judge distances. Keep a following distance of at least three seconds when riding at night.

questions.question: When riding in a group, mirrors should:

options.text: Be checked often by all riders.
Be checked only by the lead rider.
Not be checked often because they distract riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be checked often by all riders.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, check your mirrors often. This helps you watch the riders behind you and make sure the group stays together.

questions.question: The best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle is to:

options.text: Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Always look far ahead on the road while riding. This helps you spot dangers early and react to them before they become a problem.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not needed when wearing a helmet.
Is only needed for long trips.
Should be used on every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on every ride.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet on. Always wear hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: A motorcycle may pass on the right when:

options.text: There is at least eight feet of clear pavement on the right.
You ride on the shoulder of the road.
You ride on level grass beside the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is at least eight feet of clear pavement on the right.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle may pass on the right if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right of the other vehicle. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: The safest part of the lane:
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always safest. Change your position in the lane based on the conditions around you.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, helmets are:
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet whenever you ride a motorcycle.
